conventions.convention: For finite e ≥ 2, charge is 0, diagrams are English, and a node (r,c) has residue c−r modulo e. General quantum characteristic e need not be prime; symmetric-group characteristic is the prime case e=p with Hecke parameter 1.

The restricted signature reads same-residue corners top to bottom, assigns + to addable and − to removable nodes, cancels −+ pairs, deletes the first surviving −, and adds the last surviving +. Missing signs mean undefined partial moves, represented by zero in the crystal.
J is Q(q)-linear, fixes q, and sends Mλ to |λ′⟩. Transport uses Eᵢˢʸᵐ=J⁻¹E₋ᵢJ and Fᵢˢʸᵐ=J⁻¹F₋ᵢJ; conjugation preserves node type, negates residues, and reflects weights by τ.

Restrictedness means λa−λa+1<e with trailing zeros; regularity means positive-part multiplicities are less than e. Conjugation exchanges these classes. At e=0 colors are integers, every partition is a label, and no finite affine weight formula is asserted.

In Gsym(λ)=Σμ d(λ,μ)(q)Mμ, the first index is the restricted lower-basis label and the second is the ambient standard shape. Off-diagonal support requires μ strictly dominating λ, and off-diagonal coefficients belong to qZ[q].

The ambient standard frame is orthonormal. Basic upper coordinates are columns of Drect(DrectᵗDrect)⁻¹ and may be rational; integrality refers to the restricted upper dual lattice, not the ambient standard lattice. Upper bar is the adjoint bar with its own dual charts.

The canonical basic-crystal identification and full highest-weight decomposition inherit the declared Axiom of Choice. The partition-graph vertex identification and finite recursive cellular comparison introduce no Choice.

load_bearing.statement: Fix finite e ≥ 2 and charge 0, residue c−r modulo e, the top-to-bottom restricted signature, and the linear transport J Mλ=|λ′⟩ with reflected colors. Restricted and regular partition classes are exchanged by conjugation.

Conjugation intertwines modular good-node deletion and cogood-node addition on e-restricted partitions with the normalized operators of the QG empty component, with colors negated and including zero values. The same signature comparison gives the transported normalized operators on all partitions.

For finite e ≥ 2, the transported empty component is exactly the e-restricted partitions and is B(Λ₀), generated by cogood additions. With the declared Choice, the full module decomposes as ⊕k≥0 V(Λ₀−kδ)⊕p(k). In the algebraically closed symmetric-group regime e=p, soc E₋ᵢDλ′ is the James-labelled simple of the transposed good deletion whenever εᵢ(λ)>0.

For restricted λ, define Gsym(λ)=J⁻¹GQG(λ′)=Σμ d(λ,μ)(q)Mμ weightwise. The basic upper vectors are the inverse-Gram dual family inside the basic subspace; their ambient coordinates may be rational, while they form the integral upper basis in their restricted graded dual lattice.

For distinct same-residue corners of any partition, increasing row index strictly decreases column and content. Transposition sends the top-to-bottom i-node list to the increasing-content (−i)-node list, preserving signs; the identical −+ reductions select transposed good and cogood nodes.

For any field F and nonzero Hecke parameter of finite quantum characteristic e ≥ 2, recursively taking the head of residue induction along any good-deletion predecessor gives the actual Murphy restricted simple D(λ), independently of the deletion. These restricted labels form the transported B(Λ₀), with Choice inherited only for the canonical basic-component identification.

published_dependencies.used_for: English diagrams, positive row and column indices, conjugation, its involution property, and the empty partition.
Exact corner inequalities, new-bottom-row addability, and empty-diagram boundary cases in the order dictionary and worked computations.
Prime-case label definitions and the column-height proof that conjugation exchanges regular and restricted partitions; the batch explicitly extends the numerical conditions to finite e.
D(λ) ≅ Dλ′ tensor sign and its inverse dictionary, including characteristic 2, in the convention and James-labelled socle formula.
The explicitly inherited assumption in canonical component identification, highest-weight decomposition, and global-basis suppliers.
The integral sum-of-transpositions normalization, whose action is negated by tensoring with sign.
Transpositions act by −1 on sign, restriction retains the underlying vector space, and sign is trivial in characteristic 2.
The meanings of socle and head in the symmetric-group restriction formula and recursive cellular comparison.
Reversing the QG dominance support under transposition to obtain μ strictly dominating λ in the symmetric transition coefficients.

concerns.concern: The Example opens with “At e = 3, charge Λ₀”, whereas the title, Given, and convention item specify charge 0. Λ₀ is the vacuum highest weight, not the integer Fock charge. The tables themselves agree with charge 0.

alerts.finding: The published prerequisite's final proof step, line 52, ends “. ∎ [step 2.1, step 3.1]”. This puts ∎ before the justification tags; the prescribed final-step layout is punctuation followed by [tags] ∎. The dominance argument itself is sound.

seams_checked.note: The signature order, −+ cancellation, first-minus deletion, last-plus addition, and survivor counts agree with the modular suppliers. Prime-characteristic module statements are kept separate from general finite-e combinatorics. The James-labelled formula explicitly negates JM residues through sign. The general-Hecke comparison uses the independently proved cellular endpoint, without feeding Fock classification back into that endpoint proof.

The QG increasing-content signature and regular empty component are transported by linear J with colors negated; field-vector congruences are distinguished from crystal-residue equalities. The full decomposition retains Choice, and basic upper coordinates retain the inverse-Gram qualification. The convention and triangularity were also checked against [Fayers §2.3 and §4](https://arxiv.org/pdf/0906.4129) and [Leclerc–Thibon Theorem 4.1](https://arxiv.org/pdf/q-alg/9602025).

The inspected incoming citations preserve restricted labels, coefficient indexing, and dominance direction. The standard-vector expansion and Specht comparison explicitly use coordinate functionals or projected vectors π(Mμ), rather than asserting that every raw Mμ belongs to the basic module. Characteristic-zero decomposition-number identification is separately supplied; positive characteristic retains adjustment polynomials.
